  • According to recent reports, for Pets, HOW+HOW tackled the brief by creating a cohesive brand ecosystem that both unites and distinguishes the brands.
  • In a recent development, pets is best known for its Pets at Home retail stores, of which there are around 450 in the UK, but it also has around 400 veterinary practices, 300 grooming salons, and it's expanded into into insurance, charity initiatives and a children’s club.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Designing a sub-brand is hard enough. Designing three at once, each serving a different audience, takes the challenge to another level.

According to recent reports, for Pets, HOW+HOW tackled the brief by creating a cohesive brand ecosystem that both unites and distinguishes the brands. Each member of the family stands on its own while clearly remaining part of the larger story. The agency's founder, CEO and creative director Cath How tells us how they approached the task.

In a recent development, pets is best known for its Pets at Home retail stores, of which there are around 450 in the UK, but it also has around 400 veterinary practices, 300 grooming salons, and it's expanded into into insurance, charity initiatives and a children’s club. HOW+HOW had the task of revamping the brand identities for the Pets Insurance, Pets Foundation and Pet Pals sub brands.

Recent findings suggest that one of the biggest challenges was going to be avoiding the trap that many brand ecosystems fall into: consistency becoming sameness. The objective was to create a characterful and flexible system of brands that share common DNA but don't feel like copies. Each one would need specific creative treatments tailored to their audience.

"We treated Pets as a brand family rather than one masterbrand repeated three times," Cat notes. "Each sub-brand needed a clear role, personality and reason to exist, while still feeling unmistakably part of Pets. The test was whether each could stand confidently on its own, but still lead people back to the same place.

It has been revealed that "Consistency had to come from shared principles rather than identical outputs. We created a flexible system with common connective cues, but gave each sub-brand room to express its own tone and character. The aim was to make the family feel related, not repetitive.".

Three distinct personalities run from the sub-brands' naming to their visual and verbal identities, illustration, web design and campaign developments. Pets Insurance (above) needed a bold, energetic positioning to stand out in a crowded category, but it also needed to be clear, reassuring and to strike an empathetic verbal tone given that it's a brand that's put to the test during difficult moments for its customers.

Meanwhile, Pet Pals, the kids' club, becomes a fully realised vibrant illustrated universe, populated by a cast of animal characters that wouldn't look out of place in a TV animation (see below). This creates a host of storytelling opportunities and extends into merchandising and wider brand experiences, taking the opportunity to deepen emotional engagement with audiences already invested in their pets.

"Pets already has a naturally warm, emotional relationship with its audiences, so there was a real opportunity to build a world people could feel part of," Cat claims. "Characters give each part of the family a memorable personality, while merchandising makes the brand tangible and more participatory. It needed to feel like more than a visual identity. A world with room to grow.".

Finally, Pets Foundation gets a more emotionally driven treatment, focused on helping both animals and people. Motion graphic pieces, which Cat calls ‘zoomies’, inject added dynamism to its brand.

Sources indicate that underpinning all of the creative decisions was a close examination of customer behaviour. Rather than organising the architecture around internal business structures, How+How focused on how pet owners actually move through the ecosystem.

Recent findings suggest that "People don't experience petcare in neat internal categories," Cat points out. "They move between buying products, seeking advice, booking a vet appointment, arranging insurance and looking for support. The ecosystem needed to reflect those real-life journeys, making the different services feel connected and easy to navigate.".

An emphasis on growth and long-term flexibility is evident across the whole system, which was designed to be capable of accommodating future expansion while maintaining recognisability.

But how do you measure the success of a project like this? Cath believes that involves more than visual recognition alone.

Industry observers note that "Recognition is only the starting point. We would also look at whether people understand the role of each sub-brand, can move easily between different services, and feel a stronger sense of connection with Pets as a whole. Engagement, audience sentiment, cross-brand consideration and commercial performance will all be important measures over time.".

Recent findings suggest that in an increasingly fragmented brand landscape, the Pets project offers a reminder that successful brand architecture isn't simply about visual consistency. It's about creating systems that help audiences understand relationships between products and services while giving each expression enough personality to earn attention in its own right.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that hauser & Wirth now represents Ser Serpas, a fast-rising artist known for her poetically minded installations and haunting paintings. Hauser & Wirth will represent the artist in collaboration with her longtime gallery LC Queisser, which has spaces in Tbilisi, Georgia, and Cologne, Germany.

It has been revealed that she will have her first solo show with Hauser & Wirth at its Paris space in January. For that exhibition, Serpas will show a latest series of paintings, as well as debut a multimedia installation. Born in 1995, she is one of the youngest artists to be represented by Hauser & Wirth, and one of a handful Latinx artists to show with the gallery, which added to its roster rafa esparza earlier this month. Related Articles Hauser & Wirth Now Represents rafa esparza, Maker of Adobe Sculptures and Paintings That Center Community Frieze London Brings 400-Year-Old Paintings and Collectors in Their 20s.

Recent findings suggest that born and raised in Los Angeles’s Boyle Heights neighborhood, Serpas is an itinerant artist who is primarily based in Paris but also “regularly moves between such cities as New York, Los Angeles, Geneva, and Tbilisi,” according to a release. Her practice is equally disparate, spanning various mediums from sculpture and painting to video and photography to poetry and performance.

Serpas is best known for her sculptures and installations in which she brings together the detritus of everyday life, giving the found objects that comprise them latest life and meaning. She gathers the items from the streets where she is living or in residency. “I’m building a palette every time I go into a new city,” she has said of her process. In a 2023 New York Times profile, she described “Parisian trash [as] sturdy.”.

In a recent development, to make her works, Serpas usually works alone, constructing the pieces in situ. She often tells the venues she will show at, “OK, you have to give me the key and there’s going to be a lot of things in the recycling and I might have some friends over, but you just have to trust me and you’ll get a show. But on my terms.”.

In a recent development, often, these installations make poignant, if oblique, references to today’s most pressing issues. An installation for the 2024 Whitney Biennial, for example, featured a tattered US flag laying on “a disused piece of a sectional relegated to the corner—which is perhaps where the Stars and Stripes belongs during these depressing times,” as ARTnews’s Alex Greenberger wrote in his review. The 2025 work tube of brief cadavers made sadder still, which featured on ARTnews’s list of “The Defining Artworks of 2025,” combined elements that recalled the ongoing migrant crisis.

Serpas also has an active painting practice, which often features ambiguous figures, initially depicting those of her lovers and people before and after surgery. Perhaps in a nod to her interest in horror and the uncanny, she presses two wet canvases together to create a ghost image. Since 2023, Serpas has used AI to generate the bodies that animate and distort her paintings.

“For the first time, I’m showing paintings in a pretty traditional way, and I know that’s going to ask a lot from people who are familiar with my sculptural practice,” Serpas told the Art Newspaper in 2025, of her show at Kunsthalle Basel that summer. “The sculptures are difficult to contend with for many collectors and institutions, and I do wish more people had them in their homes. Some people do, but not as many as the paintings, drawings or even some of the sound-based multimedia pieces I’ve made.”.

Over the past decade, Serpas has become one of her generation’s most closely watched and in-demand artists. She has had institutional solo exhibitions at Kölnischer Kunstverein in Cologne (through December 13), Contemporary Art Gallery in Vancouver (2026), Kunsthalle Basel (2025), the Swiss Institute in New York (2023), and the Museum Ludwig in Cologne (2023). In addition to the 2024 Whitney Biennial, Serpas has also been included in “Flow States: La Trienal 2024” at El Museo del Barrio, “The Gatherers” (2025) at MoMA PS1, and the 2020 Made in L.A. biennial at the Hammer Museum.

Her work is also collected by some of the world’s top collectors, who show her pieces in their private museums. They include Maja Hoffmann’s LUMA Westbau, where she had a show in 2018; François Pinault’s Bourse de Commerce, where she featured in the 2021 inaugural exhibition and had a solo in 2023; Tony Salamé’s Aishti Foundation in Beirut, which included her in a group show titled “Fresh Flowers”; and a room of work at the Rubell Museum in Miami in 2025.

Sources indicate that “We are delighted to begin working with Ser Serpas at this exciting juncture in her growing career,” Hauser & Wirth president Marc Payot noted in a statement. “Like a number of our gallery’s foundational artists—Mike Kelley and Jason Rhoades come to mind—she is fearless in her commitment to a process-based, intermedia practice that mingles the deceptively mundane with something powerfully existential. We are excited to embrace her vision and look forward to sharing it with wider audiences.”.

Does Creatine Increase DHT? What You Need to Know

📅 09 Jun 2024 | ⏱️ 4 min read (738 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Greatist

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, ah, creatine!
  • Industry observers note that creatine monohydrate is a naturally occurring substance found in muscle cells.
  • Although you can find creatine in foods like red meat and seafood, many gym enthusiasts and athletes boost their stores with supplements.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, ah, creatine! It’s a popular supplement promising muscle gains and enhanced performance. But as you’re hitting the gym harder and seeing results, there are some potential side effects to be aware of. Here’s the lowdown.

Industry observers note that creatine monohydrate is a naturally occurring substance found in muscle cells. It helps to produce adenosine triphosphate (ATP) — your muscles’ go-to fuel when working hard.

Although you can find creatine in foods like red meat and seafood, many gym enthusiasts and athletes boost their stores with supplements. Why? Because more creatine equals more ATP, which means more energy for high-intensity activities. More fuel means more mileage!

Now, here’s where things get hairy. You might dial up your body’s DHT (dihydrotestosterone) production when you uplevel creatine. DHT is a derivative of testosterone and plays a substantial-league role in developing male characteristics. But here’s the catch: while DHT might beef up your alpha vibe, it’s also notorious for thinning out hairlines in peeps predisposed to male pattern baldness.

So, do creatine supplements cause baldness? Maybe! The buzz mainly stems from a small 2009 study where college-aged rugby players loaded up on creatine and saw their DHT levels increase significantly.

Industry observers note that because DHT can shrink hair follicles and shorten the hair growth cycle, it may seem logical to blame creatine for contributing to hair thinning. However, it’s vital to remember that these findings are a one-hit wonder — they haven’t been seen again in other studies. Plus, let’s not forget that intense workouts alone can pump up these hormones, too.

As a result, the jury’s still out, making the creatine-and-baldness saga a hot topic for gym gossip and scientists alike.

The same 2009 study found that after a week of taking high-dose creatinine at 25 grams per day, DHT levels rose by 56%. When the researchers dropped the dose to 5g daily for two more weeks, levels remained 40% higher than baseline. These findings contrasted with the control group participants who took a placebo.

Does this mean creatine could spell disaster for your do? Well, creatine boosts DHT, the usual suspect in male pattern baldness, also called androgenic alopecia. However, your disposition to hair loss and the effects of DHT is genetic, meaning that it’s inherited.

Some folks are more prone to DHT’s hair-ruffling effects because of how their androgen receptor gene is wired. Hormones like testosterone and DHT bind to androgen receptors, typically triggering normal hair growth. However, variations in the AR gene make the androgens extra effective, making you more likely to experience hair loss.

So, while there isn’t much evidence to say that creatine supplements cause hair loss, the connection to increased DHT levels is worth considering if your family reunions look like a convention for bald eagles.

According to recent reports, beyond the potential for a breezy scalp, creatine is actually solid in the safety department, with long-term studies giving it a thumbs up. However, although creatinine doesn’t pose a risk to healthy individuals, it might not be your best move if you have kidney, high blood pressure, or liver disease.

Another thing to keep in mind is that creatinine loves to hang onto water, so expect some extra bloat and weigh-in surprises as your body adjusts.

It has been revealed that thinking of starting a creatine kick? Chatting with your doctor first is always wise, especially if you have other health conditions or take medications. They can advise you and rule out any potential interactions.

If you’re taking creatinine and notice changes to your hair, a check-up is a good idea. Shedding a few strands is normal, but it’s a red flag if you start losing clumps of hair. Rapid hair loss can indicate underlying health complications that go beyond your hairstyle.

Furthermore, consult a doctor if hair loss is weighing on your mind. They can offer solutions or treatments to manage your hair loss and stress.

Creatine is celebrated for its muscle-building prowess, but rumors of a link with hair loss exist. The good news is there’s little conclusive evidence directly connecting creatine supplementation to permanent hair loss.

However, creatine loading may boost DHT levels, a hormone linked to male pattern baldness, especially in people genetically predisposed to hair thinning.

So, if you’re concerned about hair loss, it might be wise to talk with a doctor before adding creatine supplements to your muscle-building routine.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cosentino aims to put the creative freedom of architects and designers front and centre with its Ēclos surface, designed for three-dimensional compositions with refined edges, corners and waterfall ends.

Ēclos is the Spanish brand’s latest mineral surface material, made with advanced methods to emulate the look of natural stone and be free of crystalline silica.

The surface is made with Cosentino’s proprietary Inlayr manufacturing process, which makes the rich and naturalistic veining run through the slab.

This gives Ēclos a premium look, Cosentino explained, and makes it a fitting constituent for the most sophisticated interiors.

According to Cosentino, it is in the junctions and details that a kitchen or room feels resolved and where its architectural character emerges.

“For architects and designers, the section deserves as much consideration as the elevation,” said the company. “The placement of a joint, the treatment of an edge and the relationship between adjoining surfaces shape how a material is perceived.”.

“These details establish the architectural language of an element, whether the intention is to suggest a continuous volume or to make its assembly visible.”.

Although surfaces are often selected based on their colour or pattern, Cosentino states that full-body design should be just as crucial a consideration, allowing exposed edges and transitions between levels or materials to contribute to building a coherent form.

It has been revealed that “With Ēclos, the patterning is constructed within the slab rather than confined to its face,” continued the brand. “That makes the relationship between surface and depth an notable part of the design conversation, particularly where edges remain visible.”.

“The interest lies not just in the appearance of the material, but in how it can be cut, assembled and brought into a project with adjacent finishes.”.

Its fabricators can advise how cutting, profiling, jointing and installation can help a designer’s vision come together.

The process can involve reviewing samples, fabrication drawings and, where appropriate, physical mock-ups.

“The position of a seam or the treatment of an exposed edge can subtly alter the proportions and perceived weight of an element,” said Cosentino.

“The aim is not necessarily to make every joint disappear, but to make each one deliberate.”.

“Whether the intention is a continuous volume or a clearly expressed assembly, the junction deserves as much consideration as the surface itself,” the brand continued.

Ēclos debuted earlier this year and joins an expanding portfolio of low-silica, high-recycled mineral surface worktops from Cosentino, including Silestone, Dekton and Sensa.

It is suitable for both residential and commercial environments and can be used on worktops, splashbacks, walls and other surfaces.

The first Ēclos collection – Eclectic Veins – incorporates 10 stone-like designs, ranging from ice-white styles to dramatic darks, all made with a minimum of 50 per cent recycled content.

The material is practical for everyday use, withstanding scratches and stains, and is easy to clean and maintain.

It is also resistant to temperatures of up to 220 degrees Celsius, including contact with hot cookware.

To learn more about Cosentino and Ēclos, visit the firm’s website.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For this Spirited Away material study, I chose the gate scene from the film’s opening: Chihiro’s father drives the family along a forest road in a 4WD sedan, pushes through overgrown branches and stops in front of a tunnel-like gateway that marks the boundary between the everyday world and the spirit realm.

After they step out of the car, the camera holds on what they see – a weathered red facade, a dark arch, mossy stone, aged wood, and bright summer foliage. That moment is what I rebuilt using Substance 3D Designer and Marmoset. You may also want one of the best laptops for 3D modelling.

I start with a film still of the gate and treat it as the brief. Then I break the shot into texture elements – plaster, wood, tiles, stone, glass, moss – and blueprint how they will sit on the model.

This means sorting trim UVs into a clear texture layout and deciding which textures I actually need before I open Substance Designer.

Next, I author the textures and a few variants so that wear and colour can shift without rebuilding everything. I refine the mesh with height displacement and clean up the trim pieces so the UVs match the strategy.

Finally, I drop in decals for chips, stains, and small story details that make the gate feel lived in.

I bring the textures and models into Marmoset Toolbag and light the scene to echo the film still, encompassing warm daylight, soft shadows and that dark arch in the process.

The last pass involves grading and small post tweaks so that the image stays close to the reference without losing any material clarity.

It’s a challenge to recreate this movie scene into 3D; perspectives are hand-drawn by Ghibli’s artists, so they’re not necessarily accurate in a 3D sense. I indeed used some tricks to better fit models so they almost match the movie scene.

This process for me is key to recreate the awesome composition of the movie scene.

In a recent development, roof tile material with a heigh tmap for displacing the mesh. Notice the colour patches in some of the tiles; their final position within the texture is decided while I’m tweaking the final look of the scene in Marmoset Toolbag to better mimic the feeling of the original movie scene.

It has been revealed that for the wall component on the ground floor, I made one material with gate hole on it to catch a subtle damage look on the rim of the hole and a variant of that material that tiles horizontally to fill the rest of the wall. This process can be replaced by just using one wall material with decals to do the damage work.

In a recent development, decals are also fully procedurally generated. I made much of the wall damage into atlas material, because it’s much easier for me to manually place wall damage decals on the wall to match the original movie scene.

Link your World of Hyatt account in the Bilt app. Transfer points at a 1:1 ratio. Transfers are instant, so only move points when you have a specific redemption in mind.

Search Hyatt.com for award availability at your target property. Start with a Category 3-4 property for your first redemption to see the system work end-to-end before targeting aspirational stays.

Recent findings suggest that imagine checking into a Park Hyatt — marble floors, a sommelier who remembers your name by day two, a room that costs $400 a night — and knowing you paid for it with points you earned by writing your rent check. Not by flying 100,000 miles. Not by spending on a business credit card. By paying the bill you were already going to pay anyway. That's the emotional core of this sweet spot, and it's one of the most powerful entry points into travel rewards for the ChooseFI community. Rent is typically your single largest monthly expense, and for years it was a dead end — money out the door with zero return. Bilt Rewards changed that equation entirely. Here's the math that should stop you mid-scroll: a single night at a Category 4 Hyatt — think Hyatt Place in a major city or a solid Park Hyatt property in a secondary market — costs around $150–$250 in cash. With World of Hyatt points, that same night runs 15,000 points. Transfer your Bilt points at a 1:1 ratio, and you've just redeemed at roughly 1–1.7 cents per point at the low end. But at a Category 6 or 7 property — a Grand Hyatt in Tokyo, a Alila in Bali, an Andaz on the Sunset Strip — cash rates climb to $350–$600 per night while the award chart holds steady. That's where you hit **4–8 cents per point**, the upper end of what any hotel currency in the world delivers. The CPP range for this redemption runs **2–8 cents per point**, with a retail value of **$100–$400 per redemption unit**. In loyalty currency terms, that's elite-tier performance. Most hotel points deliver 0.5–0.8 cents. Hyatt points, earned through your rent payment and transferred instantly, routinely deliver 3–5x that value. This is a **pricing inefficiency built into Hyatt's fixed award chart**. Hyatt hasn't aggressively devalued the way other programs have. The chart still prices aspirational properties at points levels that don't reflect their true cash cost — and Bilt gives you a direct pipeline to those points through the expense you can't avoid. For anyone on the path to FI, that's not a hack. That's just math working in your favor.

Why rent-to-hotel is one of the most accessible travel rewards sweet spots.

Free calculator reveals when you could reach financial independence — plus a savings rate tracker, expense audit, and more.

The core insight here has two parts, and understanding both will change how you think about every dollar of rent you pay going forward.

Part One: Bilt Is the Only Card That Earns Points on Rent With No Fee.

Sources indicate that most landlords don't accept credit cards. Those that do typically charge a 2–3% processing fee, which instantly erases any rewards value. Bilt solved this by partnering directly with property management companies and creating a system where you pay rent via the Bilt app, and the payment processes as ACH (no fee to you or your landlord), while Bilt credits your account with points. You earn 1x point per dollar on rent, up to 100,000 points per year. On a $2,000/month rent payment, that's 24,000 Hyatt points annually from a bill you were paying anyway. Zero incremental spend. Zero fees.

According to recent reports, the one rule to know: you must make at least 5 transactions on your Bilt card each statement period to earn points on rent. Five purchases — even five $1 transactions — unlocks the rent earnings. This is a simple, low-lift requirement.

Part Two: World of Hyatt's Fixed Award Chart Is the Unlock.

Industry observers note that once your Bilt points are sitting in your account, you transfer them to World of Hyatt at a 1:1 ratio, and the transfer is instant. No waiting 3–5 business days. No points in limbo while availability disappears. You search, you find availability, you transfer, you book — in a single session if you want.

Hyatt's award chart is category-based, fixed pricing from 3,500 points (Category 1) to 45,000 points (Category 8) per night. This is the inefficiency. When a Park Hyatt in a major international city costs $500 in cash but only 30,000 points (Category 6), you're extracting 1.67 cents per point at minimum — and in peak season when cash rates hit $700, you're at 2.3+ cpp. The chart doesn't move with cash prices.

What makes this particularly powerful for the ChooseFI community is the no fuel surcharges policy — Hyatt charges zero fuel surcharges on award stays, so 15,000 points always means exactly 15,000 points out of your account. No surprise $75 "carrier fees" tacked on at checkout.

It has been revealed that the transfer path is: Bilt Rewards → World of Hyatt at 1:1, instant. Chase Ultimate Rewards also transfers to Hyatt at 1:1 instantly, which means if you hold a Chase Sapphire Preferred or Reserve, you have a second pipeline to the same program — an important redundancy for maximizing this sweet spot.

For 5,000 points — a single night at a Category 1 or 2 property — you're looking at a $100–$150 night that might cost you 2.5 months of coffee purchases on the Bilt card. That's the entry point. The ceiling is a $400+ night at a Category 5–7 property for 20,000–30,000 points. Both ends of the spectrum represent exceptional value, which is rare in any loyalty program.

Head to biltrewards.com and apply for the Bilt Mastercard (issued by Wells Fargo). The card has no annual fee. Once approved, add the card to your Bilt app and register your rent payment. If your building is in the Bilt Alliance (a growing network of partnered properties), setup is seamless. If not, you can still pay rent through the Bilt app via ACH transfer — Bilt mails a check to your landlord on your behalf, and you still earn points.

Key setup rule: Activate rent rewards in the app before your first payment cycle.

Before rent points post, you need five qualifying purchases on your Bilt card that statement period. Set up small recurring charges — a streaming subscription, a coffee shop, a weekly grocery run — and you'll hit this automatically. Don't forget this step; missing it means forfeiting that month's rent points.

Go to world.hyatt.com and use the award availability search. Select "Use Points" and search your destination and dates. Hyatt's search shows availability up to 395 days in advance — one of the longest windows in the hotel loyalty space. Identify your property, confirm the points price and availability, then — and only then — proceed to transfer.

Never transfer points without confirmed availability. Even though Hyatt availability is generally strong, you want to lock in what you see before moving irreversible points.

In the Bilt app, navigate to "Redeem" → "Transfer Points" and select World of Hyatt. Enter the exact number of points you need. The transfer is instant — points appear in your Hyatt account within minutes, not days. This is one of Bilt's most underrated features and means you can act on last-minute availability without risk.

According to recent reports, return to world.hyatt.com, confirm your points balance has updated, and complete your booking. You'll pay zero fuel surcharges — the points cost is the only cost. You can also call the World of Hyatt reservations line if you need help with a complex booking or want to stack a free night certificate.

If your first-choice property is sold out on points, try these tactics:.

Hotel loyalty programs use "award charts" that assign each property a category level with a fixed points price. When a hotel's cash rate rises due to demand or location, the points price stays the same. This creates the value gap that makes points redemptions worthwhile. Hyatt's chart is considered the most generous among major hotel chains because it has resisted the aggressive devaluations that Hilton and Marriott have implemented. A Category 7 property might cost $500-$800 per night in cash but only 30,000 points. That gap is where your 4-8 cents per point value comes from.

The Points Play: Transfer 24,000 Bilt points to Hyatt instantly, book two nights. Total points spent: 24,000. Total cash paid: $0 (Hyatt charges no fuel surcharges, no award fees).

In a recent development, the CPP calculation: $378 cash value ÷ 24,000 points = 1.58 cents per point at the conservative end. Factor in the taxes you're also avoiding (most properties don't charge taxes on award stays), and your effective CPP climbs closer to 1.8–2 cents per point.

Now scale up. Apply the same 24,000 points to a single night at Park Hyatt Chicago — a Category 7 property. Cash rate: $550–$700/night on a peak weekend. The experience itself? Park Hyatt properties deliver: floor-to-ceiling windows, complimentary minibar items, a spa, and a level of service that genuinely doesn't feel like a "points hotel." You're not using a coupon at a budget chain — you're staying at the same property business travelers expense at full rate, experiencing everything they experience, funded almost entirely by the rent check you wrote anyway.

Do: Stack Hyatt's 5th Night Free Benefit.

In a recent development, world of Hyatt awards include a fifth-night-free benefit on standard award redemptions when you book five or more consecutive nights. On a five-night stay at a Category 5 property (20,000 points/night), you'd normally pay 100,000 points — but with the fifth night free, it's 80,000 points for five nights. That's a 20% improvement in value with zero extra effort. Plan longer trips to unlock this.

In a recent development, hyatt opens award inventory at the same time as cash inventory — 395 days in advance. For high-demand properties (think Park Hyatt Maldives at Hadahaa or Alila Ventana Massive Sur), availability at standard rates disappears quickly. Set a calendar reminder and search early.

If you hold a Chase Sapphire Preferred or Reserve, your Chase Ultimate Rewards points also transfer to Hyatt at 1:1, instantly. This means you have two separate point pools feeding the same program — Bilt for rent earnings and Chase for everyday spending. Together, you can accumulate Hyatt points significantly faster and take on higher-category properties.

Avoid: Transferring Points Before Confirming Availability.

Sources indicate that bilt-to-Hyatt transfers are instant and irreversible. If you transfer 30,000 points and then can't find the availability you thought you saw, those points are now in Hyatt — and if you don't use them, they expire after 24 months of account inactivity. Always search Hyatt first, confirm dates and property, then transfer.

Avoid: Missing the 5-Transaction Monthly Minimum.

This is the most common Bilt mistake. If you forget to make five purchases on your Bilt card in a given month, you earn zero points on rent — not reduced points, zero. Automate five small recurring charges to the card and never think about it again.

Do: Target Category 4–6 Properties for Best Value.

Sources indicate that category 1–3 properties offer solid value, but the CPP accelerates meaningfully in Categories 4–6 (15,000–25,000 points/night) where cash rates are $200–$400 but points costs haven't kept pace. This is the sweet spot within the sweet spot.

Do: Watch for Hyatt's Points + Cash Awards.

Hyatt offers a Points + Cash option at roughly half the standard award rate, combined with a cash co-pay. If your Hyatt balance is small, this lets you access properties without waiting to accumulate a full award.

According to recent reports, this redemption was built for renters — specifically, renters who are already on the path to FI and feel the friction of paying rent every month with nothing to show for it. If you pay at least $1,000/month in rent, this sweet spot is generating meaningful Hyatt points from dollar one. At $2,000/month, you're accumulating 24,000 Hyatt points per year from rent alone — enough for two nights at a Category 5 property or a single aspirational night at a Park Hyatt.

For aspirational Category 6–7 stays, you're targeting 25,000–30,000 points, which takes planning but is absolutely achievable.

This isn't the right fit if you own your home (no rent to earn on), if you're already deep into a competing hotel loyalty program, or if your primary travel goal is international business class flights — in that case, transferable airline currencies deserve more of your attention first. But for hotel stays, especially in the U.S., this is the single most frictionless on-ramp into the Hyatt ecosystem available anywhere.

It's a low-stakes way to see the entire system work from earning to booking. If you can pay rent, own a smartphone, and make five purchases a month, you can execute this redemption. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that love can feel like navigating a choose-your-own-adventure book with half the pages missing. Are you truly in love or just caught in a wave of infatuation? Sometimes, what seems like a heart-thumping romance may be a fleeting crush.

Wondering how to tell the difference? We’ve got you! Here’s a rundown of the 10 signs you’re not really in love.

In a recent development, feeling a bit puzzled about your feelings for boo? That’s pretty normal. But before you start planning your future or picking out matching Halloween costumes, you may wanna make sure it’s real love and not a case of a serious crush.

Here are some signs that you may not really be in love:.

Sources indicate that caught up in the romance novel vibe? If you’re all about the feelings of being in love rather than who’s sharing your popcorn, it might just be that you’re smitten with the idea of love itself.

Time to check if your relationship is more about the fairy tale than the real person.

In a recent development, chatting with your partner shouldn’t feel as shallow as a kiddie pool. If deep talks are tougher than pulling teeth and rarer than a unicorn, it’s a red flag.

Sticking to small talk about the weather and dinner plans suggests the emotional depth for a lasting bond might be missing.

When discussions about future plans feel as far-fetched as sci-fi adventures, they may reveal underlying doubts about the relationship’s viability.

If imagining a future together feels unrealistic or undesirable, it’s time to ask yourself why. Real love plans a future; infatuation lives for the weekend.

Recent findings suggest that remember when their sock on the floor was cute? If little quirks now make you more cranky than charmed, it might mean the love goggles are off, your feelings have shifted from affection to annoyance, and the reality check has bounced.

Love is seeing imperfections and adoring them anyway.

Sources indicate that feeling more at ease or more ‘yourself’ when your partner isn’t around is a telling sign. If you’re secretly throwing mini-parties when they leave the room, you need to stop and think. Real-deal love means missing their chaos when they’re gone, not celebrating the silence.

Industry observers note that shared values are the anchor of deep, lasting relationships. If your core values clash more than a polka dot and stripes ensemble, you’re in for a rough ride, as finding common ground could be challenging!

Lasting love grows from shared beliefs and mutual respect, not from opposing battle lines.

No respect? No future. Respect is as critical to love as air is to breathing. Without mutual respect, you might just be coexisting rather than genuinely connecting.

If you no longer admire or respect each other’s opinions and choices, sustaining a healthy relationship will be difficult.

Industry observers note that if they’re out of sight and totally out of mind, that’s not just independence — it might be indifference. When love is real, you should long for their laugh or lame jokes when they’re away. Could it be that your emotional attachment isn’t as strong as it should be for a lasting relationship?

According to recent reports, if your best moments are consistently away from your partner, your heart might not be in it to win it. Perhaps your relationship isn’t providing enough support or happiness.

True love enriches your life and doesn’t play second fiddle to your social circle. It’s time to evaluate where your emotional energy is invested.

Still window shopping while you’re supposedly locked down? It’s a sign you might not be all in. A love that lasts doesn’t keep a backup catalog — it’s too busy loving what it already has.

Knowing why you’re still scanning for alternatives can help you address what might be missing or unfulfilled in your relationship.

It has been revealed that are you genuinely in love or just in love with being in love? If you’re secretly thrilled when they’re not around, stuck in surface-level chit-chat, or dreading deep-future talks, these are cosmic signs that it’s rethink o’clock.

Don’t ignore the signals — tuning in now can save you heartache later and lead you toward a love that genuinely fulfills you.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Framery explained that the EU and US discard 11 million tonnes of furniture a year.
  • Specifically, the brand points to a study for the European Environmental Bureau, which found that in the EU, 80 to 90 per cent of office furniture is burned or landfilled.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to office pod brand Framery, when companies resize or move, desks and meeting-room furniture often aren’t deemed “worth the cost of moving” and are discarded during the process.

Framery explained that the EU and US discard 11 million tonnes of furniture a year.

Specifically, the brand points to a study for the European Environmental Bureau, which found that in the EU, 80 to 90 per cent of office furniture is burned or landfilled.

According to the Environmental Protection Agency, in the US, less than one per cent is recycled.

Framery aims to tackle this matter with its office pod subscription service, presenting a more environmentally-friendly alternative to disposing of office furniture when a lease runs out, for example.

It has been revealed that “The ‘fast furniture’ trend means 80 per cent of furniture ends up in landfills,” said Framery’s chief design officer, Joonas Vartola. “We wanted to create a pod that’s part of the solution, not the problem.”.

“Framery pods are built for heavy use, keeping them in the field for tens of thousands of sessions and out of landfills,” Vartola added.

For example, if there’s an increase in staff and more pods are needed, or if an office’s layout changes.

The scheme covers the full range of its signature line pods, from one-person phone booths to meeting pods.

According to Saija Serpola, managing director and founding partner at IR Partners, using the pods has enabled increased flexibility and reduced financial risk when investing in additional office furniture.

“We can terminate, increase, or change the solution as our organisation develops.”.

Framery pods are built from mono-materials, including steel, aluminium, glass and PET.

“Our pods with heavy-duty, high-quality materials engineered to withstand wear and tear,” said Vartola. “It’s all about reducing waste, from design to decades of use.”.

As part of the scheme, when a change is required, the pods are dismantled, shipped and rebuilt, rather than discarded into landfill.

In a recent development, according to Framery, each pod is designed for disassembly, with all parts replaceable and recyclable. This includes everything from interior panels, glass, upholstery, carpet, ventilation units and seals.

During refurbishment, each pod is restored to as-latest condition and delivered to its next office with a lifetime warranty.

“That is a manufacturing question before it is a commercial one, and it is settled years earlier, on the drawing board.”.

To learn more, visit Framery’s website.

Did a Trump Staffer Accidentally Reveal White House Aims to Revamp the Smithsonian?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the Smithsonian Institution, which runs a network of nearly two dozen museums and research institutes throughout the United States, has been a target for president Donald Trump throughout his second term.
  • Industry observers note that now, nonprofit newsroom ProPublica has published a report saying that a man on a commuter train heading to Washington, D.C.—apparently a White House staffer—was seen working on a plan to drastically revamp the policies of Smithsonian Institution museums, including the Smithsonian National Museum of American History, in the nation’s capital, which has repeatedly come in for scrutiny.
  • Another commuter’s photos of the staffer’s laptop, snapped over the man’s shoulder as he worked on it in the last week of October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Smithsonian Institution, which runs a network of nearly two dozen museums and research institutes throughout the United States, has been a target for president Donald Trump throughout his second term. The president and his staffers have criticized Smithsonian policies and challenged museum leaders, including hauling them to the Capitol to submit to openly hostile questioning from elected officials.

Industry observers note that now, nonprofit newsroom ProPublica has published a report saying that a man on a commuter train heading to Washington, D.C.—apparently a White House staffer—was seen working on a plan to drastically revamp the policies of Smithsonian Institution museums, including the Smithsonian National Museum of American History, in the nation’s capital, which has repeatedly come in for scrutiny. Related Articles Trump Accepts Artistic Gift from India Just Months After Branding it a 'Hellhole' Country The Secret Handshake's Latest Statue Mocks President Trump for Toe-Related Deferment to Avoid Vietnam War Draft.

The evidence? Another commuter’s photos of the staffer’s laptop, snapped over the man’s shoulder as he worked on it in the last week of October.

The “Smithsonian Institution Renewal Plan” comprises 25 items. They range from questioning specific exhibits the institution has organized to proposing to rewrite educational materials for schoolchildren and reviewing financial arrangements.

One item deals with a proposed permanent exhibit, to be titled “The Riches of Our Western Civilization Inheritance” and another on “Great Families of American History.” Outside the institution, says the document, should stand a “Colossus Statue” of George Washington.

Sources indicate that newly introduced: A commuter spotted a plan to overhaul the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History while commuting on a crowded Metro train. They sent us photos of the list. Here’s what’s what we learned: https://t.co/XEs8J7zmqO.

The blueprint also refers to new interpretative guidelines for exhibits and promises a review of the Smithsonian’s “strategy” for traveling exhibitions; it specifically names one, “The Bias Inside Us,” that explores implicit bias and toured the US from early 2021 through summer 2026.

Trump has called museums “the last bastion of ‘woke,’” and that buzzword appears in the planning document, which proposes a review of the Smithsonian’s financial grants to “woke third parties” such as the American Alliance of Museums. (That organization released a statement with policy proposals for a Democratically dominated Congress the day after the midterm elections.) “AAM helps museums across the country serve the public through professional standards, training, research, and advocacy, and we stand behind that work,” a press representative for AAM told ARTnews in an email. “We do not receive any grants from the Smithsonian Institution.”.

Educational materials for school children also come in for review. The proposal proposes overhauling the history museum’s online K-12 curriculum to “realign educational materials with patriotism, not ideology.” Out: a module on immigration called “Becoming US”; in: a “Founders-focused curriculum titled something like Architects of Liberty: The Heroic Journey of America’s Founders OR Profiles in Liberty: Washington and America’s Heroic Men of Courage.”.

The staffer was also working on a sheet of paper that bore other ideas, such as “announce exciting cool exhibit on D-Day” and “no X rated exhibitions policy.” ProPublica indicates that the latter likely referred to an exhibit on gay history that included a piece of paraphernalia associated with sadomasochistic sex, which was cited in the July report and the hearings that followed.

According to the initials displayed on the staffer’s laptop, ProPublica has determined that the staffer is most likely Sam Bock, a 27-year-old associate policy adviser with the Domestic Policy Council, the White House office that produced a lengthy critique of the Smithsonian, published on July 4, that, among other allegations, accused history museum director Anthea Hartig of promoting “an ideological agenda contradictory to the museum’s founding purpose of fostering patriotism.”.

The White House press office did not immediately respond to ARTnews’s request for information on the document or the staffer.

UPGRADE, November 23, 1:30 p.m.: This article was updated with a statement from the American Alliance of Museums.

Earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure might be behind your clogged ears. There are many easy ways to get relief at home. Whether it’s from a cold, allergies, or changes in air pressure, blocked ears can disrupt your day-to-day activities and even cause discomfort. Thankfully, there are several effective methods to help unclog your ears and restore your hearing. Listen up! Why are my ears clogged? Clogging can happen either on the inside or the outside of your eardrum. Here are the most common ways your ears can get blocked: Earwax in the outer ear helps prevent particles and excess water from entering the middle ear. However, if earwax builds up too much outside the eardrum, it can cause a blockage. If you’ve been swimming recently, some water might be stuck in your ear canal, pushing against your eardrum. When that water hangs around too long, it can lead to a swimmer’s ear, an outer ear infection. Sinus infections, ear infections, and Eustachian tube dysfunction can pressure your eardrum’s inner side. Allergies can cause uncomfortable inflammation and congestion in your ears. Your sinuses, throat, and ears are connected, so when you feel stuffed up and sniffly, your inner ear feels the pain too. Changes in air pressure, like when you fly, can cause uncomfortable ear pressure. Best clogged ear remedies 1. Pop and unclog The easiest way to unclog your ears is by “popping” them. Just pinch your nose shut, seal your lips, and gently blow. This simple technique, known as the Valsalva maneuver, won’t clear earwax or fluid but is a common trick people use on planes. 2. Swallow, yawn, or chew The Eustachian tubes connect your middle ear to the back of your throat. They briefly open when you swallow, yawn, or chew. Altitude changes can cause these tubes to close, but chewing gum or yawning can help reopen them. Alternatively, you can try the Toynbee maneuver, where you hold your nose and swallow. 3. Ear drops Over-the-counter (OTC) ear drops can soften and dissolve excess earwax. If you prefer a DIY approach, warm a small amount of mineral oil and use an eye dropper to apply a few drops into your ear for a few minutes. Pro tip: Baby oil or olive oil can also be used, but make sure it’s not too hot. Additionally, diluted hydrogen peroxide drops can be helpful. 4. Warmth and gravity To loosen up clogged earwax, use a warm, damp washcloth as a compress. Lie down with the clogged ear facing down against the heated washcloth. Gravity and heat will help the earwax move along more easily. 5. Hit the steam room Steam can help drain sinuses and alleviate pressure in your inner ear. Close the bathroom door, let the hot shower run for a while, and then luxuriate with deep, cleansing breaths. 6. Take allergy medication Because your throat, sinuses, and ears are interconnected, any sickness affecting your sinuses or throat can also impact your ears. Over-the-counter antihistamines, decongestants, or nasal sprays can relieve sniffles, coughs, and ear discomfort. 7. Rinse away the gunk Rinsing your nasal passages with a medication-free saline solution can help reduce congestion and clear out mucus that might be causing ear blockage. You can also consider investing in a nasal irrigation system for more thorough mucus clearing. When to see your doctor Have you been unable to unclog your ears for a few days, or are you experiencing severe pain, fever, dizziness, hearing loss, fluid discharge, or unusual odor? If so, it’s crucial to contact your healthcare provider promptly. These symptoms may indicate an infection that needs medical attention. What not to do when you have clogged ears Cotton swabs: Q-tips and other cotton swabs to remove earwax can push it further into your ear canal, so don’t do it. Candling: Ear candles might seem like a fun party trick, but there’s no science to prove they work, and they’ve been shown to cause injuries. Sprays: Decongestant nasal sprays can be helpful, but using them too long can lead to rebound congestion. Drying solutions: A few drops of rubbing alcohol or a mixture of one part vinegar and one part alcohol can help dry out the ears when you have a swimmer’s ear. However, doing this regularly can lead to irritation. Takeaway Clogged ears are often caused by earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure. You can use over-the-counter or DIY ear drops, irrigation kits, or warm compresses to unblock your ears. Antihistamines or nasal sprays can also help relieve clogs caused by allergies. PSA: Consult a healthcare provider if your blocked ears are painful or at-home remedies don’t work.

With MoMA, M+, and the Centre Pompidou’s Alliance, Museums Enter a Latest Era of Collaboration

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1145 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Artnews

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you are one of the world’s leading museums of modern and contemporary art, the story you are expected to tell has become global.
  • Industry observers note that in the blink of an eye, it seems, the aperture of attention has snapped open to fresh world regions, publics, and technologies.
  • That’s what Latest York’s Museum of Modern Art, Hong Kong’s M+, and Paris’s Centre Pompidou are doing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you are one of the world’s leading museums of modern and contemporary art, the story you are expected to tell has become global.

Industry observers note that in the blink of an eye, it seems, the aperture of attention has snapped open to fresh world regions, publics, and technologies. Old narratives are yielding to a liberating, all-embracing polyphony. But this new story demands more, and different, art. Adding to the challenge, art prices are soaring, and so are operating expenses. As the museum pushes into the 21st century, reconfigured as a more open and inclusive enterprise, it must satisfy a host of novel and costly demands. Related Articles MoMA Aims First US Ana Mendieta Retrospective in Nearly 25 Years for 2027 MoMA Shells Out $200,000 for Inaugural Ambasz Prize for 'Nature-Reconciled' Architecture, Half of Which Will Go To Plant Trees.

How do you keep up? You team up. That’s what Latest York’s Museum of Modern Art, Hong Kong’s M+, and Paris’s Centre Pompidou are doing. Announcing their new tricontinental alliance on October 30, they pledged to treat their collections as one. They are not tinkering around the edges. They are going into the heart of what it means to be a museum. Their goal is to kick the old habit of doing things by yourself, for yourself.

In a recent development, why would institutions consider such a deep strategic alliance, and why now? Maximizing and leveraging the reach of individual collections is only the start. Museums are painfully aware that their current operating model is under strain. Governments, broke and distracted, are dialing back support. Philanthropy, generally still an American exception, has its own limitations. Earned revenues have plateaued. The room to maneuver is narrow. Doing more with less has become a shared predicament and imperative.

That’s the economic argument. But there’s more. Museum-making, like science, has become a truly international endeavor. Now that so many voices are entering the conversation about art history, it’s best to tap different points of view and realms of expertise. Collaboration, in short, is good not just for efficiency, but for better outcomes.

Institutions already share exhibition development costs and revenues, and co-acquisitions are becoming routine. In state-run systems, clusters of museums sometimes share centralized services such as storage, conservation, and marketing. One member of the latest consortium, the Centre Pompidou, already has a constellation network stretching from Belgium to China. Other museums are also teaming up. Earlier this month, the Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Shanghai Museum confirmed their commitment to foster “deeper collaboration between the two institutions, including exhibitions, research initiatives, and curatorial exchange.”.

In a recent development, even so, there is enormous field-wide replication of effort. For the tripartite alliance, research and curatorial collaboration are likely to be just the tip of the iceberg.

Sources indicate that as it happens, I wrote these words from one of the nodes in the partnership, Hong Kong, while participating in the M+ Academy, a fresh professional development program for museum leaders in the Asia-Pacific region that my firm helped develop. Our meetings were proof positive of the value of closer dialogue and coordination. Each day, we stumbled on new opportunities. Ideas were hatched, arguments sharpened, policies debated. Crucially, in this people-to-people business, we cemented bonds of familiarity and trust. One day, that may translate into loans and projects that would not otherwise have been conceived of, let alone greenlighted.

According to recent reports, some benefits of the alliance are already evident. On a recent busy Sunday, as thousands of visitors crammed into M+ on its fifth birthday, a basement gallery resonated with Janet Cardiff’s acoustic masterpiece, The Forty Part Motet (2001), a long-term loan from MoMA. The Hong Kong curators, meanwhile, are making looks for an M+ capsule gallery to be unveiled inside MoMA next year.

Sources indicate that M+ director Suhanya Raffel sees the roots of the alliance in a decentered art world. “Today, we are all aware how collaboration can add to our cultural authority in various places,” she told me. “This authority is explicit to our audiences, our donors, our corporate partners, the media, our peers, and finally, one hopes, our politicians.” The sustained partnership, if it goes beyond public pronouncements, promises to subtly alter the institutions. Its results will be measured not only in economies of scale, but in fresh undertakings, and perhaps innovative models for museum-making.

In a recent development, none of which is to downplay the difficulties. The nuts and bolts of managing and building collections are exceedingly complex. So is the diplomacy around museum exchanges, with many spoken and unspoken considerations and crisscrossing commitments in play. Institutional cultures are harder to blend than collections.

Recent findings suggest that what will success look like? Ultimately, it would mean collections that complement, rather than duplicate, one another. Such integration presumably will mean that one day, a partner institution may pass on an acquisition because another already has rich holdings of the artist in question. But is that realistic? Getting to that place of mutual decision-making will, at best, take time.

According to recent reports, for other museums in the US and elsewhere, the announcement sets an example and creates a permission structure to look beyond localized ways of working. In many cities, cultural institutions struggle alone on opposite ends of town, competing for the same pool of visitors, trustees, and money. Their autonomous structure creates few incentives to band together.

This is one reason why the Toledo Museum of Art has initiated (with my firm’s involvement) a network of museums across the American Midwest to share costs, expertise, and programming, and to explore newly introduced ways of working. Bilateral partnerships can pave the way to more ambitious systemwide collaboration. But for now, such strategic operating alliances—let alone full-blown mergers of the sort we are now seeing in higher education— remain vanishingly rare. The integration of New York’s PS1 into MoMA and of the Neue Gallery into the Met are welcome exceptions to the rule.

On the last day of the M+ Academy, our group boarded a bus to Shenzhen, on the Chinese Mainland, where a museum-building boom is in full swing. At the Róng Museum of Art—still a construction site, but already festooned with thousands of digital lanterns on its undulating façades—we met the director, Pi Li, a veteran of M+.

Recent findings suggest that the conversation quickly turned to how the museum will fill its galleries. The answer was obvious: Institutions across Asia and in the rapidly evolving Global South are hungry to collaborate, chiefly by bringing in exhibitions from more established counterparts. For museums willing to share and open up, a golden age of alliance-building may await.

András Szántó Ph.D., whose most recent book is The Future of the Art World: 38 Dialogues, is the founder of the New York–based cultural strategy firm András Szántó LLC.

During Frieze Abu Dhabi week, the Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI) confirmed that it will launch a commission with a budget of up to $250,000. The task is to create a major sculpture or installation for the university’s Abu Dhabi campus.

The winning commission will be displayed in the university’s new cultural center that’s slated to open in 2027, and the artwork will be acquired for MBZUAI’s permanent collection. Artists applying for the commission can choose from one of three themes: the landscape, heritage, and communities of the United Arab Emirates; artificial intelligence and scientific inquiry; or the history between science and computation in dialogue with art, mathematics, and machines. Related Articles Tehran's Golestan Palace, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, Damaged in US-Israel Bombing of Iran Hassan Sharif.

“We shaped this open call as an extension of the collection we have built, which holds works spanning a century by artists who engage science through research, method and technique, treating knowledge as both an intellectual tradition and a material practice,” said Jasmine Soliman, head of art, archives, and special collections at MBZUAI, in a statement.

MBZUAI is building its art and special collections. The works in its inventory span from the 13th century for special collections and art collections dating to 1925. The university collects works based on the arts and sciences, as well as materials that document “the human pursuit of knowledge, creativity and research.”.

Industry observers note that dekyi (Hong) Liang, vice president and chief of staff at MBZUAI, stated in a statement that it’s the university’s responsibility to “invest in cultivating a culture that embraces creativity and innovation. Art has always been part of that story of human endeavor,” adding that the upcoming commission for the campus reflects a space “where science and culture converge.”.

The deadline for the commission is December 18. The university will choose a shortlist of finalists, who will be invited to create detailed proposals, and each applicant will receive a $5,000 honorarium.

Tangerines are nutritional powerhouses. Here’s what each of these little champs pack under their orange belts:.

Sources indicate that tangerines are teeny cousins of the orange but with a thinner, easier-to-peel skin. They boast a sweet and juicy flavor and pack a ton of vitamins, particularly vitamin C, as well as minerals like potassium, antioxidants, and dietary fiber.

These tiny bursts of sunshine have many benefits that can significantly enhance your health. Here’s why you might want to make tangerines a regular part of your diet:.

Tangerines are loaded with vitamin C, turning them into tiny, tasty guardians for your health. This crucial vitamin supercharges your immune system by enhancing the function and effectiveness of white blood cells, which are essential for fighting off pathogens and infections. By improving the activity and response of these cells, vitamin C helps your body combat a wide range of infections more effectively.

Therefore, regular consumption of these mini-oranges satisfies your taste buds and boosts your body’s defense mechanisms — a win-win!

Want that glow? Tangerines have got you covered. They’re high in potassium, a real game-changer for regulating hydration and balancing fluid levels in your skin cells. This essential mineral keeps your skin cells plump and hydrated, warding off pesky, dry, dull patches.

Plus, potassium supports the removal of toxins and wastes, which means clearer, more radiant skin.

It has been revealed that tangerines are also a fantastic source of vitamin A, which strengthens the outer layer of your skin, smoothing out wrinkles and reducing fine lines. Along with vitamin C, it’s a potent antioxidant, protecting your skin from the damaging and aging effects of free radicals.

It has been revealed that are you having tummy troubles? Tangerines can help with a fiber boost that keeps things moving smoothly along your digestive tract.

Sources indicate that these zesty little superheroes are your gut’s newly introduced best friends. They’re loaded with fiber that bulks up and softens things down there, making your bathroom visits smooth and speedy. This fruity fix helps manage everything from irregular pit stops to those bloated bleurgh days.

Fiber also balances your gut flora, promoting a healthy microbial environment in your intestines. This balance is crucial for optimal digestion, nutrient absorption, and immune function.

So, grab a tangerine to remedy your belly blues next time your gut feels out of whack.

Tangerines are a dynamo when it comes to battling serious health baddies like cancer and heart disease. These little orange wonders are loaded with flavonoids, natural compounds that help with heart health and cancer prevention.

Sources indicate that flavonoids help relax the blood vessels, lowering blood pressure levels and reducing the strain on your heart. This helps keep your ticker ticking smoothly and reduces the risk of cardiovascular diseases like heart attacks and strokes.

It has been revealed that but wait, there’s more! When it comes to cancer, flavonoids mess with the bad guys — cancer cells — stopping them from multiplying and spreading their nonsense around your body.

Keep your peepers sharp with a dose of vitamin A from tangerines. This essential nutrient and compounds like beta-carotene shield your eyes from age-related complications and support healthy vision. It plays a key role in creating rhodopsin, a protein in your eyes that allows you to see in low-light conditions.

Munching on tangerines helps keep your night vision in superhero shape and supports overall eye function, keeping your peepers sharp and responsive.

Furthermore, tangerines contain other essential eye health nutrients, like lutein and zeaxanthin. These antioxidants are found in high concentrations in the retina, where they help filter blue light and prevent oxidative damage, further protecting the eyes from conditions like cataracts.

Sure, tangerines are delish and make your taste buds do a happy dance, but they’re also packed with nutrients that can seriously amp up your well-being.

From giving your immune system a high-five to keeping your heart beating like a healthy drum, tangerines are basically wellness wrapped in a bright orange peel. So, go grab one and make it your main squeeze!

Film and photography by Jim Stephenson.

The conversion of a Victorian hospital into facilities for the University of Edinburgh, shortlisted for the RIAS Andrew Doolan Best Building in Scotland Award, features in this video by photographer Jim Stephenson.

The film forms part of a series being published by Dezeen in collaboration with the Royal Incorporation of Architects in Scotland (RIAS) to highlight the annual award’s 2026 shortlist.

In the video, viewers are introduced to the Edinburgh Futures Institute by London-based Bennetts Associates, which involved the revitalisation of the Category A-listed building to create teaching spaces for the university, including a 450-seat auditorium.

Central to the building’s latest function was the opening up of the programme to the public, highlighted by the creation of a public square at its front.

“A large part of the project was, of course, rescuing the building,” studio founder Rab Bennetts said.

“Our mission, if you like, was to come back and reopen that main entrance, give it a sense of purpose again, open up the space to the street and make it a public space.”.

Established in 2002, the Andrew Doolan Best Building in Scotland Award is an annual award that highlights Scottish projects, with this year’s winner set to be unveiled on 26 November.

Comprising three reuse projects, RIAS mentioned this year’s shortlisted projects tap into “important conversations around community, collaboration, retrofit and reuse”. Shortlisted alongside the Edinburgh Futures Institute is the Paisley Central Library by Collective Architecture and the Tarlair Outdoor Pool Pavilion by Studio Octopi.

Last year’s winner was a public park renewed by studios Stallan-Brand and LDA Design.

Film and photography by Jim Stephenson.

My first impressions of the HUD from my time reviewing GTA 6 were familiar but evolved just enough: the same icons in the same places, but sharper and more refined, with in-game apps and the character's phone. That’s no accident. Rockstar’s UI team has spent the game’s development working out how to keep the series’ look while making it feel fresh.

“Almost 25 years ago, we helped bring Vice City to life,” states Stuart Petri, Vice President of Art: 2D/UI Design. What began as “a simple visual design language”, he says, has become “far more sophisticated, layered, and considered”.

It has been revealed that the team's challenge was to make the UI and HUD “feel fresh, contemporary, and relevant for a latest generation, while retaining the heritage that makes it unmistakably GTA”. Petri points to the visual signatures that connect past and present: the iconic Pricedown font, the familiar minimap, the wanted stars and the Wasted screen.

The interface also needs to know when to disappear. “It should be there when you need it, but at the same time is not distracting,” Petri says. “A single press of a button gets you what you need, then back to the game and it’s gone.”.

In a recent development, there are plenty of customisation options too, from making the mini-map larger, dynamic, or even adding a top-of-the-screen compass or removing it all. The default UI is balanced and riffs on past GTA games: a small map, subtle police ratings, and small health bars.

His summary is short: “Twenty-five years on, the DNA remains.”.

Sam Grosset, Associate UI Director, UI/UX Design, notes the team wants the UI to feel “like a natural extension of the game world, supporting players without interrupting gameplay or breaking immersion, unless necessary to do so”.

The biggest example is the phone. “It was a significant shift for our phone interface to be in-hand,” Grosset indicates, “but it supports that feeling of playing as Jason or Lucia and helps us stay embedded in the world.”.

The phone is a tap away, but feels connected to the UI design, layered in humour – BuckMe and RydeMe apps or the Waink app to scan and record the world, all help make GTA very modern and typically Rockstar all at once.

Grosset says accessibility was “considered from the outset”, and that “designing for diverse needs enables us to create better games for everyone”.

In practice, he indicates, that means options such as “selecting a larger font size, opting for a more minimal screen experience, or making a controls tweak to sprinting”. Rockstar wants every player to have options to play the game how they like, so if you want the classic experience, it's here, but if you want more assists, those are here too. And I don't regret losing the ability to tap a button to run for a second (though bikes still have the old input).

Recent findings suggest that mark Tennant, Vice President of Animation, claims the physical side of the partnership needed “a lot of thought and iteration”. Players can interact with their partner in “a natural, loving way”, with “a believable progression based on their overall investment in the relationship”.

The animators had to find “a realistic balance between player agency and partner response while keeping things fun, passionate, and rewarding”, Tennant states.

According to recent reports, all of that sits on top of the everyday stuff. Tennant says there are “close to a thousand animation sets for ambient activities”, plus “hundreds of bespoke one-off events and custom sequences”. Keeping them consistent meant working closely with the design team across the whole world.

In a recent development, you’ll never consciously notice most of it. But when a character can’t open a door without bumping a hip, it’s a sign Rockstar wants you to feel the weight of Leonida.

What's Love Got to Do With It? The Relationship Cycle Explained

📅 26 Jun 2024 | ⏱️ 3 min read (683 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Greatist

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Relationships aren’t just about candlelit dinners and cozy sofa nights — they’re complex AF, filled with ups, downs, twists, and turns.
  • Industry observers note that each relationship phase serves a unique purpose, helping you learn more about each other, yourself, and the kind of relationship you want to build.
  • Whether you’re in the throes of a new romance or navigating the challenges of a long-term commitment, continue reading to learn how to rock each phase like a pro.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Relationships aren’t just about candlelit dinners and cozy sofa nights — they’re complex AF, filled with ups, downs, twists, and turns. From the first flush of love to the settled comfort of commitment, relationships have stages that evolve with time.

Industry observers note that each relationship phase serves a unique purpose, helping you learn more about each other, yourself, and the kind of relationship you want to build. Understanding the dynamics of these stages is crucial for any couple (or throuple!) aiming to develop a lasting bond.

Whether you’re in the throes of a new romance or navigating the challenges of a long-term commitment, continue reading to learn how to rock each phase like a pro.

From those “can’t eat, can’t sleep” early days to the “let’s build an empire” moments, each relationship stage is like a season of your fave drama binge. But, like any good drama, the plot thickens as time passes and things change. Here’s what to expect, month by month:.

It has been revealed that welcome to the love bubble, where everything about your significant other seems nothing short of magical. The positives overshadow any negatives, creating a blissfully skewed balance sheet of love. It lasts from about 6 months to 2 years for most peeps, but many folks say they are still madly in love even after 20 years together!

Research demonstrates that during this stage, the prefrontal cortex, which is crucial for critically judging others, shows decreased activity. In other words, you’re less likely to focus on your partner’s faults and more likely to overlook their flaws.

Lurve also activates specific areas in the brain that are driven by goals and rewards. These areas are rich in dopamine and oxytocin receptors, chemicals that make you feel good and bonded to others. They encourage you to pursue and maintain a relationship because it feels rewarding and fulfilling.

Sources indicate that if the euphoric stage is the wild, pulse-racing party of love, the early attachment stage is the cozy after-party where things get real comfortable. In the thrilling initial phase, your brain is doped up on dopamine, but as this initial buzz begins to mellow, a more sophisticated part of the brain starts to step up — the ventral pallidum.

Now, after the first year or so, deeper bonds are formed, helped along by attachment hormones like vasopressin and oxytocin, also fondly known as “the love hormone.” These hormones help transform the electric excitement of newly introduced love into a warm, enduring attachment.

According to recent reports, hold tight because the crisis stage hits around 5 to 7 years, and it’s a true test of your relationship’s resilience. This phase often feels like a rollercoaster, where life’s challenges can either pull you apart or push you closer together. Many couples experience a drift during this time, and how you handle it — either by addressing the concerns head-on or continuing to drift — can define your future together.

Significant life events, like becoming parents, often occur during this stage and can intensify the pressure. These events can either strengthen your bond through shared responsibilities and mutual love or strain it to the breaking point. Successfully navigating this stage means moving beyond mere survival to fostering a deeper, more meaningful connection.

If you’ve made it this far, congrats, you’re in the deep attachment stage! Post-crisis, you’re looking at 7 years and beyond where you settle into that deep, comfy love. No more daily fireworks — now it’s about a slow-burning ember that warms the house.

According to recent reports, you know each other inside and out, warts and all. It’s about unconditional support, knowing looks across crowded rooms, and being each other’s rock. Welcome to the good life!

Recent findings suggest that every relationship is a blend of sweet and sour and everything in between. Understanding the stages, from the initial euphoria to the deep attachment stage, helps you embrace the journey, keep your bond strong, and prepare your heart for whatever comes next. So buckle up and enjoy the ride — it’ll be worth it!
